rationale: Edge-case lens (completed after initial verdict) found one critical and three major issues. EC-1 (critical): all Popup instances share the same document.querySelectorAll('[role=dialog]')[last] query, so when multiple Popups are simultaneously visible, every focus-trap listener targets the innermost dialog — outer popups lose keyboard accessibility. EC-2 (major): CSS :not() concatenation applies only to the last selector rule, not all six; filter works today by coincidence of sentinel element type. EC-3 (major): closable={!hideClose} disables PrimeReact's Escape priority queue for hideClose popups, leaving only the custom Escape handler which fires for all visible popups simultaneously. EC-4 (major): the Proxy filter and focus-escape-recovery branch go completely untested. Blind and acceptance lenses failed to run (API errors/stall).

standards_review.notes: No security surface in this diff — DOM focus management only.

findings.problem: All Popup instances share the same document.querySelectorAll('[role="dialog"]')[last] query. When multiple Popup dialogs are simultaneously visible (e.g. ConfirmationModal over a form Popup), every instance's keydown listener targets the innermost dialog. The outer Popup's focus trap is captured but redirected into the wrong dialog.
findings.impact: Any nested-modal flow (confirmation, delete, publish over another form dialog) breaks keyboard accessibility for the outer dialog entirely until all nested ones close.
findings.recommendation: Attach a real React ref to each Popup's own dialog root element instead of using a shared global DOM query. Either use a wrapper div around Dialog children, or use PrimeReact's onShow callback to capture the dialog element into a per-instance ref.

findings.problem: CSS :not() is appended by string concatenation to a comma-separated selector: `${selector}:not([data-p-hidden-focusable="true"])`. CSS does not distribute the trailing pseudo-class across commas — it attaches only to the final rule. The five preceding rules receive no filter.
findings.impact: Works today because PrimeReact's sentinels are <span> elements matching only the [tabindex] rule. A PrimeReact upgrade that renders sentinels as <button> or adds href would silently reintroduce the wrap-around bug.

findings.problem: closable={!hideClose} disables PrimeReact's internal Escape handler (conditioned on closable && closeOnEscape) for all hideClose popups. The remaining custom Escape useEffect fires for every visible Popup unconditionally. With two stacked hideClose Popups, both onHide callbacks fire on a single Escape keypress.
findings.impact: Stacked hideClose dialogs (ConfirmationModal, DeleteFolderPopup, OnboardingModal, and ~13 others) simultaneously close on Escape, potentially discarding unsaved form state.
findings.recommendation: Remove the custom Escape useEffect and rely solely on PrimeReact's closeOnEscape (already passed as a prop), which handles displayOrder priority correctly. OR keep the custom handler but guard it so only the topmost visible dialog responds.

findings.problem: The Proxy's sentinel-filtering logic and the focus-escape-recovery path (container.contains === false) are untested. All three new tests could pass even if the Proxy were removed entirely.
findings.impact: Silent regression protection gap — the sentinel filter and recovery path can break without test failures.
findings.recommendation: Add: (1) a test with a data-p-hidden-focusable sentinel verifying it is skipped during Tab wrap; (2) a test where focus is outside the dialog, Tab is pressed, and focus lands on the first element inside; (3) update the hidden test to assert document.activeElement is unchanged.
